heard: The sun and moon look identical in our sky. Most people assume they are naturally similar in size. But the sun is roughly 400 times wider than the moon. It is also 400 times farther away from Earth. That matching ratio makes both objects span half a degree. During totality, the moon covers the sun's disk completely. Artemis astronauts will even watch a 57-minute eclipse in space. That is why both distant worlds look identical in our sky.
